external_sources.title: On the Intraday Behavior of Bitcoin
external_sources.claim: Bitcoin exhibits significant negative first-order autocorrelation at 1h, 2h and 4h horizons, with stronger reversal after larger moves; mean reversion is therefore horizon- and state-dependent rather than a license for unconditional grid exposure.

external_sources.title: Bollinger Bands under Varying Market Regimes: A Comparative Study of Breakout and Mean Reversion Strategies in Bitcoin
external_sources.claim: Bitcoin breakout versus mean-reversion behavior changes across market regimes; unconditional mean reversion is especially vulnerable in sustained directional states.

external_sources.title: Dealing with the Inventory Risk: A solution to the market making problem
external_sources.claim: Market-making spread capture is offset by inventory price risk; inventory constraints are a first-order economic control when repeated entries accumulate directional exposure.

external_sources.title: High-frequency market-making with inventory constraints and directional bets
external_sources.claim: Inventory management must account for directional price expectations; symmetric exposure is economically inappropriate when directional information is present.

external_sources.title: Regime switching forecasting for cryptocurrencies
external_sources.claim: Cryptocurrency dynamics separate into materially different volatility/regime states, supporting preregistered state gating rather than one unconditional mean-reversion policy.

top3_axes.mechanism: Keep the frozen grid spacing, direction rules, exit geometry, sizing and cost unchanged, but allow new grid inventory only in one preregistered entry-time non-directional/mean-reverting regime; no-trade sustained directional states where inventory accumulation is economically adverse.
